feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital/public-sector communications roles: the positioning is clear, experience progression is logical, and the scope feels substantive. It reads polished overall, but impact would improve with more outcome-focused achievements, less duplication across skills sections, and a few wording/style fixes.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior-level brand: the header and experience consistently position you as a digital platform, governance, and communications leader.  
- Strong credibility and progression: long tenure at NACo with promotions shows growth, ownership, and domain depth.  
- Good use of scale indicators: 10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers, and named tools/platforms add substance.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable outcomes beyond scope/activity: include results such as traffic growth, engagement lifts, production savings, adoption rates, campaign performance, or operational efficiencies.  
- Reduce redundancy: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to tighten structure and save space.  
- Minor style/consistency edits: “organization-wide” is preferable to “organization wide”; keep serial comma usage consistent (“web, email, social, and multimedia” vs lists without it); “A2/Learning” reads awkwardly—use “A2 (learning)” or “Elementary (A2).” No obvious misspellings or major grammar errors.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible positioning that aligns well with the CV, but it reads slightly broad and repeats language already covered in the subtitle, competencies, and experience. It would be stronger with one concrete scale indicator and tighter phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a proof point from recent experience, e.g., “10,000+ page Drupal migration,” “3.5M annual page views,” or “50+ internal publishers.”
- Replace “building the platforms” with a sharper verb such as “leading” or “delivering” to emphasize senior ownership.
- Tighten the second sentence by grouping related areas: web modernization, governance, analytics, and AI-enabled content discovery.
- Possible rewrite: “Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience leading enterprise web modernization, governance, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Delivers scalable digital platforms, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia programs, and AI-enabled content discovery for complex, mission-driven organizations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Senior digital leader” overlaps with the subtitle “Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader.”
- “AI-enabled user experiences” is close to repeated phrasing in Core Competencies and Recent Projects.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block largely repeats the header and Topline Skills. It would be sharper if it emphasized distinctive, senior-level strengths and used tighter, parallel phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use more concise, executive-style wording and keep each item structurally parallel.
- Prioritize the most marketable recent strengths: web modernization, governance, analytics, AI search, automation, and public-sector communications.
- Consider replacing broader phrases like “multi-channel communications operations” with more senior language such as “digital communications leadership.”
- Suggested rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, dashboarding and reporting systems • Digital communications leadership across web, email and social • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia, studio and livestream production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section overlaps heavily with the header summary and all four Topline Skills blocks.
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” also repeats detail already covered in Work Experience and Technical + IT.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshots, but the block repeats themes already covered in Work Experience and Core Competencies. It will be stronger if tightened, made more parallel in style, and framed as selected examples rather than restating responsibilities.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Retitle as “Selected Recent Projects” and use consistent action/result phrasing for each item.
- Tighten wording: “Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content workflows, and bill-level AI chat to improve policy-content discovery.”
- Make project descriptions parallel and specific: “Launched a Drupal 10 campaign microsite featuring custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources, and a scalable modular architecture.”
- Standardize style and punctuation: use serial commas consistently; spell out “10-by-20-foot” instead of “10×20-foot” for CV consistency.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite development, and advocacy video series closely overlap with the current freelance and NACo experience bullets.
- “Built/Developed” repeats heavily; vary verbs or keep concise to avoid sounding repetitive.

items.title: Coleman Davis
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: colemandavis4@gmail.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads broad and overlaps with the header, competencies, and project section. Tighten it around scope, platform leadership, and 1–2 concrete outcomes or flagship initiatives.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper scope line: “Lead digital strategy, Drupal platform development, and content operations for a U.S. national membership organization.”
- Combine overlapping bullets and use stronger verbs: replace “Support,” “Build and refine,” and “Advise” with “Lead,” “Architect,” “Develop,” and “Establish.”
- Add measurable signals where possible: size of web properties, number of stakeholders/publishers, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, search improvement metrics, or workflow/production time saved.
- Example rewrite:
- Lead digital strategy, Drupal platform development, and content operations for a U.S. national membership organization.
- Architect web governance, workflows, and analytics systems that improve cross-channel communications execution.
- Build campaign microsites, modular storytelling components, and member-facing toolkits within Drupal for scalable reuse.
- Lead an AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content workflows, and user discovery experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “AI-enabled search” and the microsite work already appear in Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level.
- Governance/analytics language overlaps with the summary and NACo role; avoid repeating the same phrasing.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale signals. It will be stronger if you tighten the opening, foreground the biggest transformation outcomes, and avoid repeating channel-management points covered in the prior NACo role.

Suggested edit
- Replace the broad lead sentence with a sharper scope/result line: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management, leading enterprise modernization and audience growth.”
- Prioritize the website transformation first and make it outcome-led: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Strengthen impact language on analytics/governance: specify what improved if possible (reporting speed, adoption, decision-making cadence, publishing consistency, reduced bottlenecks).
- Condense channel oversight into one bullet and add metrics if available for email/social growth, engagement, or campaign performance.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this version strategic, not operational.
- Video studio/buildout may overlap with footer project examples; keep the CV item focused on organizational capability and scale.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more clearly about executional leadership, channel ownership, and systems built before promotion.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + distinction from the Director role: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, leading editorial execution and cross-team coordination for advocacy and member communications.”
- Tighten bullets around concrete ownership: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Reframe video impact: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Replace vague phrasing with outcomes/process language: “Built more consistent editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving coordination and content delivery.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Helped improve…” is too weak and repeats governance/workflow themes covered more strongly in the Director role.
- Avoid repeating broad channel oversight already stated in the Director entry; emphasize hands-on management and execution here.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. Make it sharper, more senior, and more clearly tied to recent enterprise/public-sector leadership.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with tighter, differentiated bullets such as:
- Enterprise digital strategy for high-volume public-sector platforms
- Editorial governance, publishing workflows, and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership across web, email, social, and video
- Audience-centered content strategy for advocacy and member engagement
- Consider swapping “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” for “Mission-driven stakeholder communications” if targeting broader digital leadership roles.
- Keep phrasing noun-based and parallel; avoid vague terms like “focused” where “strategy” or “operations” is stronger.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” repeat Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Audience-focused content planning” is also implied by multiple recent experience bullets; use this space for a more distinctive capability.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool dump and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and recent execution themes rather than repeat every tool.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters: “Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery”
- Drop lower-priority or older-signal items here, especially “jQuery,” unless it is central to current target roles.
- Consider replacing “WordPress - SharePoint - Power Pages” with “Enterprise CMS platforms (Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages)” to tighten phrasing.
- If space allows, align with recent impact: “AI-enabled search and discovery” and “CMS modernization and migration” should lead, given current consulting and director-level work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates the “Technical + IT” section; keep Topline Skills broader and save full tool lists for Technical + IT.
- “Workflow automation” and “AI-enabled search experiences” also echo Core Competencies; use slightly different phrasing to avoid repetition.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section and reads as a tool list rather than a senior, outcomes-oriented capability summary. This section should emphasize strategic analytics leadership, not just platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-first to capability-first, e.g.: “Analytics strategy and KPI design • Executive reporting and dashboarding • GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity • SEO, UX and performance analysis”
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with “Executive reporting and dashboarding” for clearer senior-level phrasing.
- Consider grouping tools to reduce list fatigue: “GA4, BigQuery and dashboarding tools (Power BI, Looker Studio)”
- If space allows elsewhere, tie to impact: “analytics infrastructure for strategic decision-making” or “insight generation for web optimization”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT; keep this version higher-level and leave the full tool list there.
- “SEO and performance analysis” may overlap with work-experience bullets unless framed here as a broad capability.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with “Core Competencies” and multiple NACo bullets. Make it more senior, tighter, and oriented to operational leadership rather than listing basic production tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Multimedia Production, Studio Operations & Live Event Delivery**
- Replace with tighter, higher-level bullets such as:
- Broadcast-quality video production and post-production  
- Livestream and hybrid event production  
- In-house studio buildout and operations  
- PTZ camera and multi-camera production workflows
- If space allows, add one impact cue tied to recent work: **Scaled in-house advocacy and event production capacity**
- Consider dropping “virtual” if “hybrid event production” already covers it; “video production and editing” can become “video production and post-production” for a more senior tone.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies.
- “Studio operations” and video/livestream experience are already evidenced in recent NACo roles, so avoid overlisting low-level tasks here.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” section. This item should either be tightened to emphasize depth in the most relevant platforms or removed if space is tight.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by demonstrated depth/recency: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- Consider adding proficiency cues only where supported by experience, e.g. “Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- If you want more impact, rename to “CMS Platforms” and keep it strictly platform names; let adjacent sections carry implementation detail.
- If space is limited, cut GitHub Pages first unless it supports a specific project or portfolio need.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This substantially overlaps with “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already includes Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, and Power Pages.
- Avoid repeating CMS modernization here; that concept is already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This section should feel more implementation-focused and emphasize current tools tied to delivery.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as a tighter, execution-oriented list: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery • Integrations: APIs, Google Tag Manager • Serverless/dev ops: Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions”
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless used consistently elsewhere; “HTML, CSS, JavaScript” is cleaner.
- If accurate, add scope or outcome in adjacent experience bullets instead of here, e.g., “built custom Drupal microsites,” “deployed workflow automations,” or “implemented tracking via GTM.”
- Put the most current/distinctive tools first: Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions, API integrations, then front-end languages.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Google Tag Manager” may also overlap with analytics/measurement; consider moving it to Data, Analytics & Optimization.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too long and mixes automation platforms with collaboration/project-management tools. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Split by function and prioritize true automation tools first: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier” then “Jira • Asana • Trello” and move Slack/Teams/Basecamp if space is tight.
- Rename to sharpen relevance: “Automation, Workflow & Project Systems” or “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools.”
- Trim lower-signal tools unless they are materially used in recent roles; keep the list focused on systems tied to process design and cross-team operations.
- If possible, reflect level of use elsewhere with impact, e.g., in recent experience: “Built cross-team workflow systems in Airtable and Power Automate to streamline editorial planning and reporting.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills.
- Slack and Teams read as generic workplace tools unless central to workflow design.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory rather than a skills line tied to the candidate’s recent email leadership. It would be stronger if framed around enterprise email/engagement platforms and ordered by likely relevance.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms
- Reorder for credibility/relevance: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If accurate, add scope qualifiers instead of just names: “enterprise email automation,” “member communications,” or “newsletter/campaign delivery”
- Example rewrite: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp (enterprise email automation, member communications, newsletter and campaign delivery)

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This overlaps with work-experience bullets already showing leadership of email/newsletter operations; avoid repeating outcomes here.
- “Engagement” is broad and may blur with social/web tools elsewhere; “Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms” is clearer.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization” and the NACo Director role. Use it to sharpen the technical stack, not restate capabilities already proven elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Tighten to tools + methods only: “GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Google Search Console • A/B testing”
- Replace vague “Dashboarding” with specific platforms already listed, or with “KPI reporting” only if that phrasing is removed from Topline Skills.
- Consider swapping “SEO” for “Google Search Console” or “SEO analysis” to make it more concrete and tool-oriented.
- If space allows, order by strongest/recent relevance: “GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • Google Search Console • A/B testing”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization”; keep one section broader and the other strictly tool-based.
- “Dashboarding” repeats what Looker Studio and Power BI already imply.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too general and overlaps with the stronger 2018–2024 NACo entries. Make this role clearly foundational: team build-out, early platform/content execution, and first-line supervision.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles as part of NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations.”
- Replace vague phrases like “high-impact” and “strengthening workflows” with concrete actions: website refresh support, livestream production, weekly video series production, channel coordination, basic process improvements.
- Clarify supervision: “Provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate” or “helped supervise a digital media associate.”
- Add 1–2 metrics if available: number of livestreams/events, cadence of weekly videos, audience growth, email/social volume, or size/timing of the website refresh.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating “weekly video updates” and broad cross-channel operations already covered in the 2018–2022 role unless you add earlier-stage context or metrics.
- Don’t reuse “built/led digital team” language that is better reserved for the more senior 2022–2024 entry.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads broadly and overlaps with later NACo roles in digital/media. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and tighten the research/program support language.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo program and policy teams; launched the organization’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with a more active, specific line such as: “Produced multimedia and digital content to support member communications and policy storytelling.”
- If possible, add scope or outcome: number of episodes launched, audiences served, teams supported, or how the podcast/content supported advocacy or member engagement.
- Keep this entry to 1–2 lines since later NACo roles carry more strategic weight.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating generic multimedia/video language already covered in the 2015–2024 NACo roles.
- Don’t overstate digital leadership here; save team-building, channel ownership and operations language for later positions.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills list, but it mixes software with capabilities and repeats multimedia themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize tools only, with the strongest, most current production capabilities implied elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Rename or refocus as tool-based only: “Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator”
